title: Simultaneous-shift and scalar normalization for coinduced complexes
statement:
Let $P\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $U$ termwise restriction of scalars, and $I$ an unbounded K-injective $P$-complex representing $P[0]$ in $D(P)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Set $V=\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(A[0],I)$ with $(a h)(b)=h(ba)$ and write $T$ for the evaluation-at-one isomorphism of [lem-trf-coinduction-total-hom-model]. Use product total Hom [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex] and shifts $(L[n])^i=L^{i+n}$, $d_{L[n]}=(-1)^n d_L$. For arbitrary complexes $L,M$ over either ring and every $n\in\mathbf Z$, the formula
$$\sigma^r_{L,M,n}(f)^i=(-1)^{nr}f^{i-n}$$
defines a natural chain isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(L[n],M[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(L,M)$. Its degree-zero action is the usual inverse shift on chain maps. Shifts preserve K-injectivity, and $J(I[n])=V[n]$ as $A$-complexes, where $J(K)=\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(A[0],K)$. These identifications represent the canonical shift comparison $C(P[n])\cong C(P[0])[n]$ for the K-injective coinduction construction $C$ [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. The maps $T$ commute with simultaneous-shift comparisons. The map
$$m_n:A[0]\longrightarrow U\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(V[n],V[n]),\qquad m_n(a)(h)=a h,$$
is a chain map, and the following equality holds as actual chain maps:
$$\sigma_{UV,I,n}\circ T_{V[n],I[n]}\circ m_n=\delta_I,\qquad \delta_I:A[0]\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(UV,I),\quad\delta_I(a)(h)=h(a).$$
No boundedness, perfectness, flatness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0BZW (lemma-relative-dualizing-algebraic), proof of (1)(c), simultaneous-shift cancellation; evaluation-at-one normalization from Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint) and 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext).

proof.text: Write $\epsilon=(-1)^n$ and let $f$ have Hom degree $r$. In the product Hom of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], reindexing $j=i-n$ identifies the factors $\operatorname{Hom}(L^{j+n},M^{j+n+r})$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(L^i,M^{i+r})$. Thus $\sigma^r(f)^i=\epsilon^r f^{i-n}$ is linear, with inverse $\tau^r(g)^j=\epsilon^r g^{j+n}$ since $\epsilon^{2r}=1$. For the differential on the shifted Hom one has $(d'f)^j=\epsilon(d_Mf^j-(-1)^r f^{j+1}d_L)$, with all differentials reindexed. Consequently $\sigma^{r+1}(d'f)^i=\epsilon^{r+2}(d_Mf^{i-n}-(-1)^r f^{i+1-n}d_L)=(d\sigma^r f)^i$. This proves the chain-isomorphism assertion over either ring, using products without any support restriction.

proof.text: For chain maps $u:L'\to L$ and $v:M\to M'$, the $i$th component of $\sigma^r(v[n]fu[n])$ is $\epsilon^r v^{i+r}f^{i-n}u^i$, which is the $i$th component of $v\sigma^r(f)u$. This gives naturality in both variables. For $r=0$ the sign is $1$; a degree-zero cocycle is precisely a chain map by the differential in [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. Hence the induced map on chain maps is the usual inverse shift, with no sign.

source.place: Tag 0BZW (lemma-relative-dualizing-algebraic), proof of (1)(c), shift cancellation; Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint), 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext), coinduced K-injective model. Explicit signed calculations supplied by Q06.

proof.text: Interpret [def-pur-kinjective-complex] on the one-object identity-cover ringed site of the chosen ring, so its module sheaves are ordinary modules. Let $K$ be K-injective over either ring and let $f:N\to K[n]$ be a chain map with $N$ acyclic. The cohomology definition in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $H^j(N[-n])=H^{j-n}(N)=0$, since multiplying a differential by $\epsilon$ does not change its kernel or image. The maps $g^j=f^{j-n}$ form a chain map $N[-n]\to K$: $d_Kg^j=\epsilon g^{j+1}d_N$. By [def-pur-kinjective-complex] choose a null-homotopy $k$ with $g^j=d_Kk^j+\epsilon k^{j+1}d_N$. Set $h^i=\epsilon k^{i+n}:N^i\to K^{i+n-1}$. Then $d_{K[n]}h^i+h^{i+1}d_N=d_Kk^{i+n}+\epsilon k^{i+n+1}d_N=f^i$. Thus every such $f$ is null-homotopic, proving K-injectivity of $K[n]$.

source.place: Tag 070H (definition-K-injective), definition and following paragraph: translates of acyclic complexes are acyclic. Explicit shifted null-homotopy supplied by Q06.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-coinduction-total-hom-model], $J(K)^i=\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K^i)$ with differential $h\mapsto d_Kh$ and action $(ah)(b)=h(ba)$. Therefore $J(K[n])^i=\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K^{i+n})=J(K)[n]^i$, and both differentials are $h\mapsto\epsilon d_Kh$; the $A$-actions also coincide. The identification is natural because for every chain map $q:K\to K'$ both maps $J(q[n])$ and $J(q)[n]$ are postcomposition with $q^{i+n}$. In particular $I[n]$ is K-injective by step 3 and represents $P[n]$, since localization commutes with shifts by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The K-injectivity clause of [lem-trf-coinduction-total-hom-model] also makes $J(I[n])$ K-injective over $A$. The K-injective construction of [def-trf-derived-coinduction] computes $C(P[n])$ by $J(I[n])$ and $C(P[0])[n]$ by $J(I)[n]$. Its shift comparison is induced by the just-verified natural chain identification. This is also the evaluation-normalized comparison: under the identity identification its counit sends $h$ to $h(1)$ on both sides, exactly the shift of the unshifted counit in the transposition $T$ of [lem-trf-coinduction-total-hom-model].

proof.text:
More generally take any $A$-complex $E$, $P$-complex $K$, and degree-$r$ cochain $f:E[n]\to J(K[n])$. Identify $J(K[n])=J(K)[n]$ by step 4. For $x\in E^i$, the formula for $T$ in [lem-trf-coinduction-total-hom-model] gives
$$\bigl(\sigma^r_{UE,K,n}T_{E[n],K[n]}(f)\bigr)^i(x)=\epsilon^r f^{i-n}(x)(1)=\bigl(T_{E,K}(\sigma^r_{E,J(K),n}f)\bigr)^i(x).$$
Linearity of evaluation at $1$ gives the middle equality, so the square commutes in every Hom degree as actual chain maps. Taking $E=V$, $K=I$ gives the asserted compatibility.

source.place: Tag 0BZW (lemma-relative-dualizing-algebraic), proof of (1)(c), shift cancellation; Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint), 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext), coinduced K-injective model. Explicit signed calculations supplied by Q06.

proof.text: Put $W=V[n]$. The model theorem [lem-trf-coinduction-total-hom-model] makes $V$, hence $W$, an $A$-complex. Because $A$ is commutative, multiplication $\mu_a:h\mapsto ah$ is $A$-linear, and $a\mapsto\mu_a$ is $P$-linear. Its Hom differential is $d_W\mu_a-\mu_a d_W=0$ since $d_W$ is $A$-linear. By [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex] each $\mu_a$ is thus a degree-zero cocycle. Sending $A[0]$ to these cocycles, and taking zero components in other source degrees, defines exactly the chain map $m_n$.

source.place: Tag 0BZW (lemma-relative-dualizing-algebraic), proof of (1)(c), shift cancellation; Tags 0A70 (lemma-right-adjoint), 0A71 (lemma-RHom-ext), coinduced K-injective model. Explicit signed calculations supplied by Q06.

proof.text:
For $a\in A$ and $h\in (UV)^i$, the composite in the statement, evaluated in its sole nonzero source degree, is
$$\bigl(\sigma^0_{UV,I,n}T_{V[n],I[n]}(m_n(a))\bigr)^i(h)=(ah)(1)=h(1a)=h(a).$$
Here $h$ on the shifted side lies in $V[n]^{i-n}$, the degree-zero sign in step 2 is $1$, and both evaluation and the action are those of [lem-trf-coinduction-total-hom-model]. This is $\delta_I(a)^i(h)$, so the maps agree in every component. The composite is a chain map by steps 1, 5 and 6, hence so is the displayed $\delta_I$. The calculations use neither bounds nor finiteness, flatness, perfectness or Noetherian assumptions.
